ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Egg A is quickly knocked toward another completely identical stationary egg B, and as a result, each time it is the struck egg B that is broken. At the instant egg A collides, in what direction will the egg white inside it, due to inertia, exert a force on the shell of egg A?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: At the instant egg A collides, the egg white inside it, due to inertia, will exert a forward force on the shell of egg A.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two completely identical eggs, the one on the left labeled B and the one on the right labeled A. The velocity arrow v above egg A points to the left, indicating that egg A moves from right to left and strikes the stationary egg B on the left; therefore for egg A, the side facing B, that is, the left side, is the “front” of the motion. Reasoning: At the instant of collision, the front end of the shell of egg A is first hindered by egg B and rapidly decelerates; but the egg white inside egg A, due to inertia, still tends to maintain its original state of motion and continues moving left along the original direction of motion of egg A. Thus the egg white, relative to the shell, will press toward the front end of egg A, exerting a force on the shell of egg A along the original direction of motion. In the figure, this direction is to the left, that is, forward, toward B.
